title: Augmented finite descent data for oriented nearby cycles
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $Y_\bullet$ a simplicial object of $\operatorname{Sch}/X$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ and $c\in\mathbb Z$. Use the actual vanishing topoi, exact constant-coefficient inverse images, derived direct images, adjunctions and canonical ordinary nearby-cycle comparison $\beta$ of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Write $\epsilon_i:Y_i\to X$, $f_i=f\epsilon_i$, $K_i=\epsilon_i^*K$, $A=R\Psi_fK$ and $T_i=R\bar\epsilon_{i,*}R\Psi_{f_i}K_i$. Define the canonical component augmentation $A\to T_i$ as the adjoint of $\beta$ for the square $(\epsilon_i,1_S)$. Define an augmented finite descent datum to consist of a cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] starting on page $1$, identifications $E_1^{i,j}\cong H^j(T_i)$, vanishing $E_r^{p,q}=0$ for $p<0$ or $q<c$ on all pages, and decreasing filtrations $F$ [def-sp-filtration] on $H^n(A)$ with $F^0=H^n(A)$ and $F^{\max(0,n-c+1)}=0$. For $0\le p\le n-c$ specify $\operatorname{gr}_F^pH^n(A)\cong E_{\max(1,n-c+2)}^{p,n-p}$; this is a stable page by the support condition. The augmented edge $H^j(A)\to E_r^{0,j}$ lifts to cycles, passes under homology to the next edge, is the canonical component augmentation on page $1$, and agrees on the stable page with the filtration quotient in degree zero. A base-change datum consists of a Cartesian scheme square $(h,g):f'\to f$ and a simplicial map $Y'_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$ over $h$ whose augmentation squares are Cartesian. For this datum define the comparison on $T_i$ by ordinary base change for $\bar\epsilon_i$, then $\beta$ on $Y_i$, then the canonical identification of coefficient pullbacks. The oriented inverse-image square is the unique comparison compatible with both oriented projections; its module lift is the generator-normalized square of the existing constant-coefficient construction. A comparison of augmented finite descent data is a morphism from exact inverse image of the old spectral sequence to the new one, with this specified first page, abutment map $H^n(\beta)$, commuting augmented edges, maps of filtration steps, and compatible maps on quotients and stable-page identifications. Allow a further coefficient map $h^*K\to K'$ and postcompose each specified comparison with it. For two base-change data, define a successive base change by a Cartesian square and Cartesian simplicial degree squares commuting over $X,S,Y_\bullet$; the coefficient identification is the canonical localized inverse-image composition, uniquely normalized on scalar insertions. To read bounded constructibility on the original small etale site, use restriction of scalars along the canonical constant-ring isomorphism, the fixed-ring module equivalence [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves], and the inverse of the $\operatorname{AsSmall}$ site equivalence. This reading functor is additive and exact. These definitions assert no existence of a descent datum.
